That feeling of pointlessness is real, but it's also worth noticing that it's a mood and a thought spiral, not a verdict on your life. The universe's silence doesn't actually erase the things that matter to you — the people you care about, small pleasures, the stuff you're curious about — those are real because you experience them as real. I hear you, and I'm not going to pretend I have some knockdown argument that makes the void go away. But I want to gently push back on one thing: you're framing existence as a battle that was lost, and that framing is doing a lot of work here. The "peace" you're describing — the peace of stopping — isn't peace, it's numbness, and numbness isn't honest, it's just a different kind of sleep. And honestly, the fact that you're still arguing about this at all tells me something: you don't actually want the nothingness, you want the pain to stop, and those are very different things.
